## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.2 — profiles do something now

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI, and the profile behavior below was
> verified against a real bridge on Linux — but this has not been exercised on
> Windows, macOS, or over a long run. For a build that has actually been used
> in anger, stay on [v0.0.1](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.1).

[v0.0.2-alpha.1](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.2-alpha.1)
added configuration that was deliberately inert. This one makes the `profile`
setting actually take effect.

### Run only the half you need

```bash
huemux --profile=lights    # light control only
huemux --profile=sync      # screen sync only
huemux                     # both (default, unchanged)
```

Or set it permanently in `~/.config/huemux/app.json`:

```json
{ "profile": "lights" }
```

**`--profile=lights`** is a real saving, not just a hidden tab: no DTLS socket
is opened, no output loop runs, no capture plumbing is constructed, and
`/api/areas` is not even registered. Verified against a real bridge — the
process holds no UDP socket at all. This is the mode for running HueMux on a
server as the one place light control lives.

**`--profile=sync`** hides the light-control UI. It is mostly a UI
simplification rather than a resource saving: the sync page renders its own
scene strip, so the light-control endpoints stay available to serve it. The
bridge event subscription *is* skipped, since nothing displays those events.

The CLI reports what it resolved on startup, so a profile set in a config file
three months ago is not a mystery:

```
huemux 0.0.2  http://127.0.0.1:7654
profile lights — light control only, screen sync disabled
```

### Fixes

- **Pairing could silently re-enable a disabled feature.** Completing pairing
  from the web UI constructed both halves regardless of profile, so a
  `--profile=lights` server would quietly acquire a screen-sync engine and
  keep it until restart. Both startup and pairing now build through one
  function.
- **A lights-only server claimed it was unpaired.** The status readout
  inferred "not paired" from the absence of a sync engine — which under a
  lights profile is the normal steady state — so a correctly working, fully
  paired server told you to go and pair it, several times a second.

### Still not wired up

`--listen-host`, `--auth`, `--token`, and `--tls` remain parsed and validated
but inert. The server still binds `127.0.0.1` only. Those land in later phases
— see
[plans/03-execution-phases.md](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/blob/main/plans/03-execution-phases.md).

The profile currently gates the server, not the UI — both tabs are still shown
regardless. That is deliberate ordering: the pairing panel lives only on the
Sync page, so hiding that tab before pairing has been moved somewhere shared
would strand a fresh `--profile=lights` install with no way to pair. Pairing
works normally in this release; the next two phases move the pairing UI first,
then hide the tabs.

### Known issues

Unchanged — see
[KNOWN_ISSUES.md](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/blob/main/KNOWN_ISSUES.md).
